architecturalPatterns.di: Hand-rolled Service Locator (DIContainer) — static registry, singleton-per-type, eager-register in Bootstrapper
architecturalPatterns.gameLoop: MonoBehaviour Bridge Pattern — GameDriver.Awake() inits singletons, Update() calls Tick()
architecturalPatterns.decoupling: C# events (OnDialogueStarted, OnLineChanged, etc.) with subscribe in Start() / unsubscribe in OnDestroy()
architecturalPatterns.actions: Stateless strategy classes (MoveAction, JumpAction, etc.) sharing ActionContext (state object)
architecturalPatterns.chapterSystem: IPositionable interface + Progression singleton discovers MonoBehaviours via FindObjectsByType
architecturalPatterns.dataModel: ScriptableObjects for all config/settings data (ActionSettings, CardData, DialogueEntry, etc.)
architecturalPatterns.puzzle: Event-driven plain C# class (Puzzle) + MonoBehaviour components (PuzzleObject, PuzzleTrigger)
architecturalPatterns.input: InputHandle wraps Unity Input System, with enable/disable for mode switching

architectureIssues.title: Service Locator Anti-Pattern
architectureIssues.detail: DIContainer is a static service locator — dependencies are implicit. Any code can call Get<T>() without declaring its dependencies. No constructor injection, no interface registration, no unit-test-friendly substitution.
architectureIssues.suggestion: Consider constructor injection or a proper DI framework (Zenject/Extenject/VContainer). At minimum, pass dependencies via Init() parameters.

architectureIssues.title: Tight Static Coupling to Singletons
architectureIssues.detail: Every system calls Dialogue.Instance, Progression.Instance, PlayerState.Instance, Gui.Instance, GameplayScene.Instance, Puzzle.Instance directly via static property + DIContainer.Get<T>(). No abstraction boundaries — UI knows about dialogue, dialogue knows about player state, player state knows about GUI.
architectureIssues.suggestion: Introduce interfaces for core services (IDialogue, IProgression, IGui) and pass them via Init().

architectureIssues.title: GameDriver God Object
architectureIssues.detail: GameDriver is responsible for: initialization orchestration, ticking all systems, event subscription management, holding scene references for ALL systems, and puzzle input lifecycle. Violates Single Responsibility Principle.
architectureIssues.suggestion: Split into per-system drivers or use a feature-flag initialization pipeline.

architectureIssues.title: Puzzle.cs Not Found
architectureIssues.detail: Puzzle class is referenced by Bootstrapper, GameDriver, and PuzzleTrigger via Puzzle.Instance and DIContainer.Get<Puzzle>(), but no Puzzle.cs file exists under Assets/Scripts/. This will cause a compile error.
architectureIssues.suggestion: Create Assets/Scripts/Interaction/Puzzle/Puzzle.cs or verify if it was accidentally deleted.

architectureIssues.title: Duplicated Camera/Input Mode Switching
architectureIssues.detail: Both GameplayScene.HandleDialogueStarted/Ended and PuzzleTrigger.HandlePuzzleStarted/Exited implement identical camera swap, cursor lock, and input enable/disable logic. This is copy-paste code — adding new modes will require duplicating again.
architectureIssues.suggestion: Extract into a shared GameModeStack or ModalInputManager that handles push/pop of input modes.

architectureIssues.title: FindObjectsByType in Warm Paths
architectureIssues.detail: GameplayScene calls FindAnyObjectByType<InputHandle>() every time dialogue starts or ends (HandleDialogueStarted, HandleDialogueEnded). Similarly in Bed.SleepSequence and NPC methods. Find operations are expensive — should cache references.
architectureIssues.suggestion: Cache InputHandle, NPC references as fields in GameplayScene or use a register pattern.

architectureIssues.title: No State Machine / Scene Management
architectureIssues.detail: Game state is ad-hoc: CurrentChapter int, puzzle IsActive bool, dialogue IsDialogueActive bool. No explicit game state machine or scene loading manager. Chapter advancement and puzzle transitions are fire-and-forget with no validation.
architectureIssues.suggestion: Introduce a GameState enum (Exploring, Dialogue, Puzzle, Sleeping...) and a state stack for structured transitions.

patternIssues.title: DIContainer Re-registration Leak
patternIssues.detail: When Inject<T>() is called for an already-registered type, it Disposes the old cache entry but the old _instance reference could still be held by external code. Only the static slot is nulled.
patternIssues.suggestion: Replace Cache<T> with proper factory-based registration that allows lifecycle management.

patternIssues.title: IReadOnlyList Wrapping Mutable List
patternIssues.detail: PlayerState.OwnedCards returns _ownedCards.AsReadOnly(), which only prevents adding/removing. The card ScriptableObject instances inside are still mutable by external code.
patternIssues.suggestion: Return a copy or use System.Collections.Immutable if appropriate.

patternIssues.title: Inconsistent Namespaces
patternIssues.detail: Some files use root namespace 'Settings' (folder-level), others use 'Assets.Scripts.Settings'. Similarly 'Utility' vs 'Assets.Scripts.Utility'. Creates confusion about assembly boundaries.

patternIssues.title: Event Subscription Lifecycle Risk
patternIssues.detail: Subscriptions happen in Start(), unsubscriptions in OnDestroy(). If a GameObject is deactivated (SetActive(false)) without being destroyed, OnDestroy won't fire and event handlers leak — the GC can't collect the subscriber.
patternIssues.suggestion: Use weak event pattern, or ensure OnDisable also unsubscribes.

patternIssues.title: Coroutine Not Stopped on Deactivation
patternIssues.detail: NPC.ApplyExpression starts BlendToExpression coroutine. If NPC is deactivated mid-blend, the coroutine continues running or silently fails. No cleanup on OnDisable.
patternIssues.suggestion: Track coroutine references and stop them in OnDisable.

patternIssues.title: Mixed Serialization Attributes
patternIssues.detail: GameDriver uses [SerializeReference] for _dialogSettings (polymorphic serialization) but [SerializeField] for all other fields. No clear rationale for the difference.
patternIssues.suggestion: Use [SerializeField] consistently unless polymorphic substitution is intended.

patternIssues.title: Chapter System Uses FindObjectsByType for Discovery
patternIssues.detail: Progression.Init() calls FindObjectsByType<MonoBehaviour>() and filters for IPositionable. This is expensive and fragile — newly spawned positionables won't be found unless RegisterPositionable is called explicitly.
patternIssues.suggestion: Use an explicit registration pattern (RegisterPositionable) or a ScriptableObject event channel for discovery.

positivePatterns: Plain C# singletons (not MonoBehaviours) for core logic — testable, no scene lifecycle dependency
ScriptableObjects for data-driven settings — enables designer iteration without code changes
Event-driven decoupling between Dialogue ↔ GameplayScene ↔ Gui — works well for cross-system communication
Stateless action classes with shared context — clean separation of input handling from game logic
IPositionable interface for chapter system — polymorphic positioning of any actor
Coroutines used for sequenced visual effects (fade, teleport, footprint reveal) — appropriate use

lochagos-di-refactor-plan.approach: Two-phase: Phase A (parallel interfaces + compat layers) → Phase B (teardown of old infrastructure)

phases.0: Define 6 interfaces in Assets/Scripts/Interfaces/ (IGui, IDialogue, IPlayerState, IGameplayScene, IProgression, IPuzzle)
phases.1: Leaf services (Level 0) implement interfaces, keep static Instance for compat
phases.2: Dependent services (Level 1) accept interface refs in Init(), replace internal static calls
phases.3: Create ServiceHub temporary container, refactor all consumers to use ServiceHub.XXX instead of XXX.Instance
phases.4: Delete Bootstrapper, DIContainer, static Instance props, ServiceHub — GameDriver becomes sole composite root with new T() + explicit Init() wiring

lochagos-di-refactor-plan.notes: Puzzle.cs must be created first (currently missing). GameDriver becomes composite root. ServiceHub is temporary — deleted in Phase B. No DI framework required for 6 services.
